teaser: Onboarding for synthetic users: invented personas, a sub-agent each, a real browser one screenshot at a time, all in a vault you publish.
core_idea: To learn what a website looks like to each kind of buyer, a Claude session reads a vault describing invented personas, their role, personality, direction of travel and mission, starts one sub-agent per persona, and each drives a real browser one screenshot at a time without reading the page's code, recording questions, confusion and actions, then is interviewed; Claude maps the findings. It is not user research, but three runs found things no test had. To start: buy a key on sgraph.ai or ask, install sgit, create the vault, keep the vault key with a key keeper, and publish the read key on any site that embeds the vault.

quotes.text: You can ask real people, and you should.
Putting the protocol in the vault is what makes a second run in a month comparable rather than merely later.
A run with no confusion anywhere is a run that was not done properly.

figures.caption: From a vault of personas to a published answer: one Claude session, one sub-agent per persona, a real browser.
One vault holds the whole study: who the personas are, how they run, every run, and the app that shows it.
